newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Discount Bank offer to be for warrants.
newsitem.headline: Discount Bank offer to be for warrants.

text.p: A secondary offering for Israel Discount Bank, slated for February, is likely to consist entirely of warrants sold by tender, a source close to the offering said on Tuesday.
"This is what's being proposed now but it isn't final," the source told Reuters, saying underwriters were examining the proposed terms.

Under a draft prospectus sent to underwiters by MI Holdings, the government company charged with selling the Israeli government's bank shares, the offering will be for warrants priced deep in the money, the source said. Holders would be able to exercise the warrants over a period of months.

The offering is expected to be for about 15 percent of Discount and to raise approximately 500 million shekels if the warrants are fully exercised. Only about 100 million shekels of the total would be paid at the time of the offering.

MI Holdings is experimenting with warrants as a way of floating the banks at a time when the Israeli stock market is in the midst of a long slump. "Secondary offerings are still pretty difficult," the source said.

Last March Discount, Israel's third-largest commercial bank, made an initial public offering (IPO) for 14.5 percent of equity (fully diluted) in one of the only major offerings of the year. The government raised $71 million from the share tranche and will raise another $80 million if the warrant tranche is fully exercised.
Foreign investors took a big portion of the IPO, but the source said he was not sure they would be as interested in an offering of warrants only.
